reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about oxidation behavior and mechanisms in multiprincipal-element alloys, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers basic selective oxidation concepts, but the specific application to MPEAs and the claimed link to mechanical integrity require supporting citations which are absent.
premises: Preferential formation of a continuous, adherent oxide scale occurs in MPEAs at high temperature
This oxide scale governs both oxidation resistance and mechanical integrity
Al and Cr are the primary oxide-forming elements responsible for the protective scale
The protective scale limits oxygen ingress and metal ion diffusion, slowing oxidation
Higher Al/Cr content leads to lower oxidation rates and better property retention
